source_text: quod si malum esset concupiscentia, careret ea qui baptizatur Deinde paulo post: Et ego, inquit, fratres, non potui loqui vobis quasi spiritalibus, sed quasi carnalibus
pass_a_gloss: That/which if evil would-be desire, careret she/it who baptizatur then paulo after: and ego, he-says, fratres, not potui loqui to-you as-if spiritalibus, but as-if carnalibus.

lemmas.lexica: LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: Do not be mistaken: neither the sexually immoral nor those who serve idols will possess God’s kingdom. (1 Corinthians 6:9–10)
And that is what you were; but you were washed, but you were sanctified. (1 Corinthians 6:11)
If sexual desire were an evil, the person who is baptized would be free of it.

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.
